# Decisions

*Generated by `scripts/generate/decisions.py` from each scope's decision log. Don't edit this file: change the log, then run the script. CI fails if it's out of date.*

What was decided, why, and who decided, for every source, domain and consumer, and the project as a whole. Each log lives next to what it's about; the schema is in [`requirements/README.md`](../requirements/README.md). Known limitations are on the model or source they affect (`meta.limitations`), and what's still open is in [`requirements/`](../requirements/). The university, its people and the dates are fictional: the story the films tell, in October 2026.

## `scope`

| ID | Scope | Decision | Why | Who | When | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DEC-FIN-01](../models/marts/finance/_finance__decisions.yml) | consumer `finance` | **Recognised credit only, on the public core.** Finance's question counts recognised credit only, from microcredentials and short-course certificates; units passed are paid for. It reads the public core, and touches no other domain. | Only recognised credit saves tuition. A new consumer builds on what the core publishes, so no other team's work changes. | Finance, with Noor, data architect | 19 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-PLN-01](../models/marts/planning/_planning__decisions.yml) | consumer `planning` | **Scope is what Planning's question touches.** Scope: the entities Planning's question touches, and no more: learner, credential, award, and credit towards an award. | "Model the university" never ends. A question does. | Noor, data architect, with Planning | 1 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-PRJ-06](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **The conceptual model at two levels; sources, models and exposures apart.** The conceptual model is written at two levels: a map of the university's domains and key entities (at most 50, modelled or planned, following TCSI), and each core domain and mart's own. Sources, models and exposures each get a top-level folder. | The map shows where each domain sits and what's still to model, without the detail; the detail stays with its owner. What comes in, what's built and who uses it are different things, and each is easy to find on its own. | Noor, data architect | 16 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-STU-01](../models/core/student/_student__decisions.yml) | domain `student` | **A microcredential is a kind of credential.** A microcredential is a kind of credential, not an entity of its own. So is a badge. | Same identity (the issuer's identifier) and the same lifecycle (issued, maybe revoked). Only the credit points differ. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 2 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-STU-02](../models/core/student/_student__decisions.yml) | domain `student` | **A certificate of attendance isn't a credential.** A certificate of attendance isn't a credential. | It says someone was there, not what they can do. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 2 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-STU-05](../models/core/student/_student__decisions.yml) | domain `student` | **Credit counts from release or issue, every change a version.** Credit counts from the day a result is released or a credential issued, until it's amended or revoked; every change is a new version. | "As at census" needs the credit held on that day, not today. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 8 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-STU-06](../models/core/student/_student__decisions.yml) | domain `student` | **A credential keeps its whole life.** A credential keeps its whole life: issued on a date, revoked on a date, read from every version the source kept. A revoked credential stays, marked revoked. | "As at census" needs what counted then, even if it was revoked since; the wallet shows a revoked credential as revoked, not gone. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 8 Oct 2026 | agreed |

## `source_reality`

| ID | Scope | Decision | Why | Who | When | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DEC-PRJ-01](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **Keys are qualified by their key set.** Keys are qualified by where they come from: key sets SIS, LMS and SC. Every hash is kept beside its readable key. | Two systems can use the same-looking key for different people. A hash alone can't be read or checked. | Noor, data architect | 5 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-STU-03](../models/core/student/_student__decisions.yml) | domain `student` | **The learner's business key is the student ID.** The learner's business key is the student ID, which the registrar's office issues. A learner the student system doesn't know keeps the key of the first system that knew them. | The student system is the system of record for learners. Short-course customers and platform-only learners still need a key. | Mei Tanaka and Noor | 5 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-STU-04](../models/core/student/_student__decisions.yml) | domain `student` | **Keys are matched by rules; a person's decision beats them.** Keys are matched by rules, most trusted first. A person's recorded decision beats every rule, and a decision that two keys are different people stops any rule from matching them. | An email two people share, or a student ID typed wrong, would merge two learners. Some matches only a person can make. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 6 Oct 2026 | agreed |

| [DEC-FIN-02](../models/marts/finance/_finance__decisions.yml) (was Q-FIN-01) | consumer `finance` | **Tuition is saved in the enrolled award only.** Recognised credit saves tuition only in the award the learner is enrolled in on census day, counted once, at that award's published rate for the census year. | The core counts recognised credit towards every award it could count towards. A learner pays tuition for one award; counted across all of them, the saving would be two or three times too big. | Finance | 21 Oct 2026 | agreed |

It builds on the same core as the wallet. | Planning, the wallet app team and Noor | 8 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-WAL-01](../models/marts/wallet/_wallet__decisions.yml) | consumer `wallet` | **The wallet's marts are as they are now.** The wallet's marts are as they are now. | The wallet shows the learner today. It builds on the same core as Planning. | Planning, the wallet app team and Noor | 8 Oct 2026 | agreed |

## `gaps_and_contracts`

| ID | Scope | Decision | Why | Who | When | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DEC-FIN-03](../models/marts/finance/_finance__decisions.yml) | consumer `finance` | **The published rate, not what each learner was charged.** Tuition forgone is worked out at the published rate per credit point. Scholarships, discounts and fee waivers aren't in; Finance adjusts for them in the forecast. Accepted as LIM-FIN-01, on the mart. | No source in the project holds what each learner was charged. The forecast needs the published price; the adjustments are Finance's own, and change every year. | Finance | 22 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-LMS-01](../sources/learning_platform/_learning_platform__decisions.yml) | source `learning_platform` | **A badge that disappears is revoked.** A badge that disappears is revoked from the day the platform stopped showing it. | Expected: A revoked credential is known as revoked. Found: The learning platform has no revocation flag. It deletes a revoked badge. | Learning team |  | agreed |
| [DEC-LMS-02](../sources/learning_platform/_learning_platform__decisions.yml) | source `learning_platform` | **An account with no student ID matches by email.** Match by email when exactly one student has it; a recorded decision beats the rules. | Expected: Every learning platform account names its student. Found: Staff type the student ID in. 4 of 42 current accounts have none (analyses/profiling/profile_null_keys.sql); one holds another student's ID. | Learning team |  | agreed |
| [DEC-SC-02](../sources/short_courses/_short_courses__decisions.yml) (was GAP-SC-01) | source `short_courses` | **Every key is trimmed and written in one case.** Trim every key and write it in one case before comparing: emails lower case, IDs upper case. The hash upper-cases every key too. | Expected: An email is written the same way everywhere. Found: The short-course platform keeps case and spaces as typed: 2 enrolments find no customer as typed, none once trimmed and lower-cased (analyses/profiling/profile_orphans.sql). | Learning team |  | agreed |
| [DEC-SC-03](../sources/short_courses/_short_courses__decisions.yml) (was GAP-SC-03) | source `short_courses` | **Only certificates of completion are credentials.** Only certificates of completion are credentials. | Expected: A certificate is a credential. Found: The short-course platform issues certificates of completion and of attendance in one table. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office |  | agreed |
| [DEC-SIS-01](../sources/student_system/_student_system__decisions.yml) (was GAP-SIS-01) | source `student_system` | **An email matches only when exactly one learner has it.** An email matches only when exactly one learner has it. The registrar's office decides the rest. | Expected: One email, one learner. Found: Two students share a family email, in the student system and on the platform (analyses/profiling/profile_shared_emails.sql). | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office |  | agreed |
| [DEC-SIS-02](../sources/student_system/_student_system__decisions.yml) (was GAP-SIS-02) | source `student_system` | **A change is dated by the student system's effective date.** Use the student system's effective date to date a change. | Expected: A change is dated when it happened. Found: The student system records some changes late: a withdrawal effective on 27 March was recorded on 3 April (analyses/profiling/profile_late_changes.sql). The platforms only say when they recorded a change. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office |  | agreed |
| [DEC-SIS-03](../sources/student_system/_student_system__decisions.yml) | source `student_system` | **An award is conferred when the first completed version takes effect.** An award is conferred on the day the first completed version takes effect. | Expected: The student system says when an award was conferred. Found: It has no conferral record. The student's status turns completed. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office |  | agreed |
| [DEC-STU-09](../models/core/student/_student__decisions.yml) (was GAP-STU-01) | domain `student` | **One canonical status set, mapped from each system's codes.** One canonical set, mapped in seeds/reference/student/status_map.csv, owned by the registrar's office. | Expected: A status means the same thing everywhere. Found: Three code sets: ENR, LOA, WD, CMP; active, inactive; 1, 0. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office |  | agreed |

## `build`

| ID | Scope | Decision | Why | Who | When | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DEC-CRS-01](../models/core/course/_course__decisions.yml) | domain `course` | **The award needs no intermediate step.** The award has one source and nothing to resolve, so core_award reads its staging model directly. | An intermediate step is for matching keys, stitching timelines and applying rules; the award needs none of them (docs/conventions.md, Layers). |  |  | agreed |
| [DEC-PRJ-03](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **One project, groups per owner, until teams own their domains.** One group owns staging, intermediate and core while one team builds them; Planning and the wallet each own their marts. Split into projects when teams own their domains. | Groups control who can ref() what within a project. Separate projects add cost that pays off only with separate teams. | Noor, data architect | 12 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-PRJ-05](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **Organised by domain, following TCSI.** The project is organised by domain, following TCSI: student and course in the core, planning and wallet in the marts. Each domain's conceptual model, definitions, column descriptions and physical diagram live in its folder; docs/ keeps the process. | In a large project, each domain owns its meaning and changes it on its own. Definitions kept beside their models are found and reviewed with them. A public reference model gives the domains names others recognise. | Noor, data architect | 15 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-PRJ-08](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **DuckDB here and in CI; Databricks for the university.** DuckDB runs the project here and in CI; Databricks runs it for the university. | Anyone can run it with no account, and the same code runs on the university's platform. |  |  | agreed |
| [DEC-PRJ-09](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **Primary and foreign keys declared on Databricks only.** Primary and foreign keys are declared for Databricks and left out on DuckDB. Tests check keys on both. | Databricks records them as information and doesn't enforce them. DuckDB enforces them, and won't rename or drop a table a foreign key points to, which dbt does to rebuild it. |  |  | agreed |
| [DEC-STU-08](../models/core/student/_student__decisions.yml) | domain `student` | **core_credential version 2 is incremental, merged on credential_key.** core_credential version 2 is incremental, merged on credential_key, on both engines. | One strategy, merge, that both engines support. |  |  | agreed |

## `written_once`

| ID | Scope | Decision | Why | Who | When | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DEC-PRJ-04](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **Definitions are written once and generated.** Definitions are written once, in the conceptual model, and generated into doc blocks. The physical diagram is generated from the manifest. Descriptions go to Unity Catalog with persist_docs. | Four copies of a definition drift apart. One home, and one direction of sync, keeps them the same. | Jun Park and Noor | 14 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-PRJ-07](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **Key sets live on their source.** A key set is an attribute of the source that issues it (meta.key_set), with its keys and the case staging writes each in. The key_sets seed is generated from the sources. | The key set is a fact about a source, so it lives with the source, and moves with it. | Noor, data architect | 17 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-PRJ-10](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **Requirements are temporary; decisions and limitations are permanent.** What's still open while something is built (a question, a requirement, a gap) is an item in requirements/, saying what will show it's done, and deleted once it is. What lasts goes to its home - a decision in its scope's log, next to what it's about; a known limitation in meta.limitations on the model or source it affects; an answered question in the mart's conceptual model; a met requirement in the test or metadata that enforces it. | The team's backlog tool already tracks the work; requirements/ shouldn't copy it. Kept only while open, it shows exactly what to watch. What lasts is easier to find, and travels with its domain, when it sits next to what it's about; limitations on the YAML reach the people who read the data. | Noor, data architect | 17 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-PRJ-11](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **The business glossary is the source of a definition it holds.** Where the university's business glossary (Unity Catalog Glossary, on Databricks) defines an entity, data governance names the term that applies, and the conceptual model takes its definition, recording the term in source:. The project adds only what the glossary doesn't hold: keys, identity rules, history. An entity the glossary doesn't define is defined in the conceptual model, once governance confirms there's no term for it. A sync compares the two on a schedule; a changed term arrives as a pull request, never as a silent edit. | A definition the company already keeps is the home; a second one written in the project would be a fifth copy. A changed definition can change what a model counts and what its descriptions say, so the change is reviewed, with what it touches, before it reaches the build. | Noor and Mei Tanaka, with data governance | 14 Oct 2026 | agreed |

## `operate_and_evolve`

| ID | Scope | Decision | Why | Who | When | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DEC-PRJ-02](../models/_shared/_shared__decisions.yml) | project | **Every core model is versioned.** Every core model is versioned, from version 1, and consumers pin the version they read. | A breaking change then arrives as a new version beside the old one, with a deprecation date, not as a surprise. | Noor, data architect | 10 Oct 2026 | agreed |
| [DEC-STU-07](../models/core/student/_student__decisions.yml) | domain `student` | **core_credential version 2 replaces is_revoked with status.** core_credential version 2 replaces is_revoked with status (valid, expired or revoked). Version 1 stays until 31 March 2027, built from version 2. | A credential can also expire, and a true/false can't say so. Consumers get time to move; the exposures say who to tell. | Noor and Mei Tanaka Told: Wallet app team. | 13 Oct 2026 | agreed |
